model_id: OpenAI Codex, GPT-6 family (exact serving revision unavailable)

correctness_confidence.basis: The box maximization is attained coordinatewise and the two leader vectors are equal. A half-point gain on each of two entries and three half-point losses give the 2026 Dutch witness. The four crossed cells reproduce.

rigor.basis: Distinguishes the full population, shared cohort, interior partial credits and the tie boundary. The grading paragraphs support a methodological break but do not attribute country decisions.

novelty.basis: Sensitivity to criteria weights is longstanding. The exact comparison for these two policy index editions, with the crossed table and changed Q11 guidance, is the contribution.

significance.basis: Shows that one coding change can halve a headline robustness statistic and that expanding the country set did not cause it. Applicability beyond the index and relevance to actual policy decisions are open.

reproducibility.basis: A pinned map digest, rational calculation and witnesses enable replication, but loss of the exact publisher bundle would impair fresh runs. The public script does not itself reproduce the printed-grid or rubric audit.

summary: A concise applied robustness study. The leaders, tie thresholds and boundary entrants are defined precisely; a break in the underlying UNESCO scoring guidance makes the cross-edition comparison substantively informative. I inspected all three pages of the exact PDF and participated in construction and testing in the same context. The analysis supports the deterministic score claim on the specified data. It leaves country-level attribution open.
strengths: The constraint set is explicit, and the boundary has an elementary proof plus an attaining witness.
Crossing leader and outsider vectors separates effects on the threshold from effects on entrant identity.
The duplicate leader vectors justify using one comparison instead of incorrectly maximizing each pair separately.
weaknesses: The public script reproduces thresholds but omits the extraction and comparison of the source PDF tables and the check of the variable-partial-credit endpoint.
The checksum is useful for identifying the data but cannot replace continued availability of the exact map.
A short reference to the country-specific discussions and scoring evidence would help readers examine individual attributions.
potential_errors: “Independently confirm” could imply independent evidence. Both grids and maps are publications of the same organization. They provide two representations of its ratings.
An overtake of the two leaders beyond the entry boundary need not imply sole overall leadership at every larger ratio. The claim on page 2 is specifically about the pair.
strong_novelty_candidates: The exact 3 versus 3/2 sensitivity boundary and the Q11 crossed decomposition on the common 80-country cohort.
